title: The Easy question in the test
subtitle: 习惯自律 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 习惯自律（生活与学习·良好习惯与自律）
meta: 主题语境：习惯自律（生活与学习·良好习惯与自律）　|　核心词汇：easy　|　正文 336 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 easy 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1960 the researcher wrote of ① an easy question in the test in the paper, and everybody in the lab said at once that it was ② easier than the one named there the year before. Three terms on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the researcher, who never explained anything, had done it before dawn and gone home; it was the easy ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the easiest question in the test anybody in the lab had ever seen, or so the paper for February 1954 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too easy to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the student who had come to help; the easy ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the tube at the far bench, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ an easy life in the south, and said that no student in his right mind would call it ⑥ as easy as the life in the south they had once had in the old lab. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was easy or not, and he said so.

By 1967 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the paper. What the line asked for was ⑦ something easy, and nothing besides. The student from the next lab called the whole plan ⑧ quite easy; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the paper kept the names of the easy ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1970, in public, she wrote of another easy question in the test in the same paper, and the work, which took two terms, seemed ⑨ easier than anybody had expected. ⑩ The easiest life in the south in the whole lab, she said in 1972, was the one she could never quite name; the easy ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 容易（前置定语 an easy question in the test：1960 年研究员在研究报告里记下的那件容易的易题）
B. adj. 容易／安逸（比较级 easier than：文中两处，一处比测验里的易题，一处比预想）
C. adj. 容易／安逸（最高级 the easiest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 容易（表语 too easy to do：母亲觉得它太容易，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 安逸（前置定语 an easy life in the south：叔叔把整件事称作一桩安逸的日子）
F. adj. 安逸（同级比较 as easy as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩南方的安逸日子相比）
G. adj. 安逸（后置定语 something easy：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 安逸（受程度副词修饰 quite easy：那位学生的评价）

items.q: an easy question in the test
the easiest question in the test anybody
an easy life in the south
The easiest life in the south in

answers.why: easy 意为“容易”，1960 年研究员在研究报告里记下的是“一件容易的易题”，此处作前置定语 an easy question in the test。
easy 意为“容易”，此处用比较级 easier than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
easy 意为“容易”，研究报告上 二月 那行字说它是实验室里最容易的一件，故用最高级 the easiest question in the test。
easy 意为“容易”，母亲认为这件东西“太容易了，谁也用不上”，too easy to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
easy 意为“安逸”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩安逸的日子”，此处作前置定语 an easy life in the south。
easy 意为“安逸”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩南方的安逸日子一样安逸”，同级比较用 as easy as。
easy 意为“安逸”，研究报告上那半行字要的是“安逸的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something easy。
easy 意为“安逸”，邻实验室来的那位学生认为这套计划“相当安逸”，quite 修饰原级 easy。
easy 意为“安逸”，1970 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要安逸”，故用比较级 easier than。
easy 意为“安逸”，母亲 1972 年说的是“整个实验室里最安逸的那一桩”，故用最高级 the easiest life in the south。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1960 年，研究员在研究报告里记下了一件容易的易题。（an easy question in the test）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更容易。（easier than …）
母亲觉得它太容易，谁也用不上。（too easy to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩安逸的日子。（an easy life in the south）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩南方的安逸日子一样安逸。（as easy as …）
到了 1967 年，研究报告上只剩半行字：要的是一件安逸的东西。（something easy）
answers: In 1960 the researcher wrote of an easy question in the test in the paper.
Everybody said it was easier than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too easy to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business an easy life in the south.
He said nobody would call it as easy as the life in the south they had once had.
By 1967 the paper asked for nothing but something easy.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 easy 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1960 the researcher wrote of an easy question in the test in the paper, and nobody forgot it.
It was the easiest question in the test in the lab, or so the paper says.
My mother thought it too easy to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business an easy life in the south, and nobody argued with him.
The student from the next lab called the plan quite easy, and everybody laughed.
The easy ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
